foundAndFixed: REAL BUG, not caught by tsc, lint, or the existing 747-test suite (none of which exercise component behavior -- confirmed earlier this session that this repo has zero React-component-render tests). packages/ui/src/components/Menu.tsx's MenuItem only extended native ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> and spread {...props} onto the <button> with no explicit handling of an 'onSelect' prop. React's ButtonHTMLAttributes DOES include a real, unrelated native 'onSelect' DOM event (fires on text selection, essentially never on a plain button) -- so it type-checked cleanly. apps/shell/src/components/SuiteHeader.tsx wired THREE of the five relocated controls via onSelect={...} (Command palette, Sign out, the SwimCloud reference-window toggle) -- all three would have been silently non-functional buttons in the shipped app: clicking them does nothing, no error, no warning, nothing in any automated check catches it. The agent's own final report directly contradicted the actual diff on this point (it claimed 'I used onClick-style native props rather than a separate onSelect prop', which was false for the code it had just written) -- caught only by reading the real diff line by line rather than trusting the summary.
